questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That it was possible to take classes in English, and that it was somewhere with both an exiting history and affordable living.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. The host university was very helpful, and there wasn't really a language barrier. Also they helped with housing for those of us who looked into it early.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not really that much. But that is also because it wasn't necessary

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Write to casa LUISS

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Find something through casa LUISS and close to campus

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You receive an e-mail when it opens, but the date is also on the website. Also they have a planning device that allows you to see if any courses overlap which is very helpful.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The schedule device

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure to do it right away so you avoid the classes filling up. It's not much of a problem unless you don't do it at the beginning, but if you don't it might become one

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It's extremely easy to get good grades, and the level isn't very high. Also 1/3 of classes are online which is anoying.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: All of the courses were part of MA programmes, but it was still very very easy

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More classroom teaching and fewer lectures

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Energy and Climate change policies, Comparative public policy in Europe, Comparative Politics, International relations of Europe, and Social and Labour market regulation

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of them were fine. Social and Labour market regulation maybe.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I lost my phone so i had to get a new one

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Cocktails, wine, resteurants, busses, metros, coffee, cake. Basically anything you can eat or drink.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Good football tournament

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The ESN Super League, a lot of different activities besides that also, but that was by far the best one. They also do a welcoming week, and my best advice for that is not to buy the full pack and wait for them to put the reduced ones up for sale

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The ESN Super League. Great way to hang out

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Bars and ruins

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Climate is nice and people are lovely

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I didn't do it really.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The local students seem pretty immature as many of them still live at home and are somewhat younger than the regular peers from back home. So that part was sort of wierd. Also cheating on exams is widely accepted (also by teachers), which is a bit uncomfortable maybe, but it's easy to just choose not to partake.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The night life

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Get housing through Casa LUISS, don't start biking around, rent a car with your frind and clime Cono Grande

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: You can write Casa LUISS the moment you have your confirmation that KU will nominate you. You don't have to wait for a letter of acceptance or anything.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Making new Danish friends

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: It can be kinda hard to be far away from everyday life. Inbetween all the fun you have a lot more time to yourself.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Bring good books

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
